title: Forces Vocabulary
keyIdea: Forces have clear names: push and pull; stretch, squash and twist for shape; touch forces versus gravity and magnets; friction and air resistance that slow things down.
familyTip: On a walk name forces: 'push the swing', 'pull the door', 'friction on your shoes', 'gravity pulls you down the slide'.

visual.caption: Match each scene to a force word. Drag, or tap a card then a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: push/pull, stretch/squash/twist, gravity vs contact, friction/air, match words.

kid: A push moves something away from you. A pull brings it toward you.
Stretch makes something longer. Squash makes it shorter. Twist turns it.
Some forces need a touch. Gravity and magnets can pull without touching.
Friction and air resistance are forces that slow things down.
adult: Force words: push, pull, twist, stretch, squash; touch forces vs forces at a distance (gravity, magnets); friction; air resistance. Link each word to something your child feels.
Common mistakes: calling every hand action a push; thinking gravity needs a touch; saying friction makes you go; swapping stretch and squash; saying air resistance is not a force.
In the lab your child pushes and pulls a car, stretches a spring, drops with gravity, slides with friction, and matches the force words.

practice.prompt: Opening a drawer is usually a…
practice.hint: The drawer comes toward you when it opens.
practice.explain: Pulling brings the drawer toward you; that is a pull force.

practice.hint: Longer means the force named stretch.
practice.explain: Stretch is the force action that increases length.

practice.prompt: You give {n} equal pushes. How many push forces is that?
practice.hint: Count each push as one force action.
practice.explain: {n} pushes means {=n} push actions in this count.

practice.prompt: A sled needs {n} friction reminders to stop. How many?
practice.hint: Friction is the slowing contact force each time.
practice.explain: You name friction {n} times; that is {=n} friction reminders.

practice.prompt: Order: name forces on a slide.
practice.hint: Start the motion, fall with gravity, then slow.
practice.explain: Push starts you; gravity acts down the slide; friction slows you.

pool.hint: Gravity pulls without needing a hand on you.
pool.explain: Gravity is a non-contact force acting at a distance.

pool.prompt: A sled slowing on snow meets…
pool.explain: Friction is the contact force that opposes the slide.

pool.hint: Weight is the pull of gravity on a mass.
pool.explain: Weight is the gravitational force on an object.

pool.prompt: Kick a ball away: that is a…
pool.hint: The ball moves away from your foot.
pool.explain: A kick away from you is a push.

pool.prompt: You name {n} non-contact examples. How many?
pool.hint: Gravity and magnets are typical non-contact examples.

pool.prompt: Squash clay {n} times. How many squash actions?
pool.hint: Each squash is one shape-changing force action.
Think of a parachute slowing as it falls.
pool.explain: Air resistance is a force that opposes motion through air.

items: name friction or gravity when it fits
pool.hint: Feel first, then sort by contact, then precise names.
pool.explain: Start from felt pushes/pulls, then contact type, then exact words.
